function.name: user_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a user based on the provided user name and the status of the mandates. This API is intended for use by partners to retrieve information about their clients' mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the partner's client for whom to fetch mandates.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If omitted, mandates of all statuses will be retrieved.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a partner based on the specified status. If no status is provided, all mandates are retrieved. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If left empty, mandates with any status will be retrieved.

message.content:
A **mandate** (in finance/wealth‑management terms) refers to a formal instruction or authorization given by a client to a financial institution—such as a bank, investment firm, or wealth manager—to manage specific assets or execute particular transactions on behalf of the client. Key points: | Feature | Description | |---------|-------------| | **Purpose** | Enables professional management of investments, savings, pensions, etc., while keeping legal ownership with the client. | | **Types** | • *Investment Mandate* – instructions on how funds should be invested.
• *Pension/Savings Mandate* – directives regarding contributions and withdrawals.
• *Estate/Mortgage Mandate* – arrangements for estate planning or mortgage payments. | | **Legal Basis** | Usually governed by a signed agreement outlining scope, fees, performance benchmarks, risk tolerance, reporting requirements, and termination conditions. | | **Client Control** | Clients retain ultimate control; they can modify or cancel the mandate at any time per contractual terms. | | **Mandate Status** | Commonly tracked as `active`, `pending` (awaiting approval), or `inactive` (completed/cancelled). | In practice, when you see “partner mandates” or “user mandates,” it’s referring to the set of such agreements managed under a partnership or belonging to a specific individual.
